title: When is the HCF the same as the common multiplier?
description: Four pairs of numbers are each a common multiplier times two other numbers. The highest common factor is the multiplier times whatever the other two numbers share, and it equals the multiplier only when they share nothing. Keeko doubts this and thinks it is always the common multiplier.
teaching_notes: One idea: the highest common factor is the common multiplier times what the other two numbers share, so it equals the multiplier only when they share nothing but one. Watch for students who always give the common multiplier as the answer.

source: Find the HCF of 18 × 10 and 18 × 15, 10 × 38 and 10 × 21, 5 × 13 and 5 × 20, and 12 × 16 and 12 × 20. In which is the HCF the common multiplier?
video_script.why: The child found that fourteen times six and fourteen times nine share more than fourteen and now tests four pairs to see when the multiplier is the whole answer.
video_script.substitution: Find what the other two numbers share, and multiply it by the common multiplier.
video_script.anchor: Four pairs in a column, each written as a common multiplier times two other numbers: 18 × 10 and 18 × 15; 10 × 38 and 10 × 21; 5 × 13 and 5 × 20; 12 × 16 and 12 × 20.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the highest common factor is always the common multiplier, but in the first pair ten and fifteen share a five, so the answer is eighteen times five.
video_script.payoff_line: The highest common factors are ninety, ten, five and forty eight

final_answer.value: (a) 90 (b) 10 (c) 5 (d) 48; the HCF is the common multiplier in (b) and (c)
final_answer.spoken: ninety, ten, five and forty eight

never_show: 18 as the HCF of the first pair, marked right
maths_rules: 18 × 10 and 18 × 15: 10 and 15 share 5, so the HCF is 18 × 5 = 90
10 × 38 and 10 × 21: 38 = 2 × 19 and 21 = 3 × 7 share nothing, so the HCF is 10
5 × 13 and 5 × 20: 13 is prime and 20 = 2 × 2 × 5, they share nothing, so the HCF is 5
12 × 16 and 12 × 20: 16 and 20 share 2 × 2 = 4, so the HCF is 12 × 4 = 48
the HCF equals the common multiplier when the other two numbers share nothing but 1: in the second and third pairs
video_script.design: One idea: the highest common factor is the common multiplier times what the other two numbers share. The four pairs stay in the anchor band all video and each step lights the pairs it uses.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We must find the highest common factor of four pairs. Eighteen times ten and eighteen times fifteen. Ten times thirty eight and ten times twenty one.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Five times thirteen and five times twenty. Twelve times sixteen and twelve times twenty.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The number in front of both is called the common multiplier.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>In which pairs is the highest common factor the common multiplier itself?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the highest common factor is always the common multiplier.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That works only if the other two numbers share nothing. In the first pair, ten and fifteen share a five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Eighteen times five is ninety, which is more than eighteen. If they share a factor, the answer is bigger.
